source.title: SimSMoE: Toward Efficient Training Mixture of Experts via Solving Representational Collapse
source.authors: Giang Do; Hung Le; Truyen Tran

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures similarity and collapse among experts within sparse mixture-of-experts models, not convergence between independently trained models or the cross-model behaviors named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CKA-based similarity results for within-model expert pairs (rows R1–R4). Language-modeling and downstream task scores for SimSMoE and comparison methods are excluded because they report task performance, not representational similarity. The cited findings from other work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The paper measures CKA similarity between experts inside one sparse MoE model, i.e. 'representation collapse', and trains to reduce it. These experts are not independently trained models or seeds, so no version is tested. It cites Li et al. 2016 (Convergent Learning) and Kornblith et al. only as background for CKA. 'cites_only' fits better than 'discusses', since the paper does not discuss the convergence claim itself.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors conclude that CKA reveals representation collapse among SMoE experts, and that the SimSMoE similarity loss mitigates it while improving pre-training and fine-tuning performance across architectures. They note larger-scale validation is needed.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses CKA to measure and reduce similarity among experts within an SMoE; it does not reproduce the original claim's cross-model alignment method or test its cross-model prediction.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported similarity patterns vary with the number of shared tokens and with layer order. The paper recommends an RBF-CKA bandwidth range of [0.8, 0.9], but does not report a comparison of convergence outcomes across similarity measures.

fits_no_version.finding: Within an SMoE, CKA similarity between expert pairs correlates strongly with the number of tokens they share (Fig 4a). In Brainformer, deeper layers show lower expert similarity (Fig 4b).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within-model expert representational similarity rises with shared input tokens and falls with depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Without a diversity loss, experts' hidden representations become more similar (Fig 5a); a CKA-based loss is intended to reduce this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MoE experts trained jointly drift toward similar representations unless explicitly diversified.

record.peer_reviewed: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Findings of NAACL 2025)
record.problems: The authors report experiments on medium-scale datasets and medium-scale Transformer-family models, citing computation limitations. The similarity outcomes in Figures 4 and 5 are presented as plots or heatmaps without reported numeric values or uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version results were reported. Task-performance tables and plots were left out because they do not measure representational similarity.

untested.parts: All: no cross-model alignment versus scale.
All: no comparison across seeds of the same architecture. Within-model experts share one training run and router.
All: no mapping or stitching between models.
All: no interpretable features compared across models.
All: no comparison of convergence across metrics. RBF bandwidth advice concerns loss stability only.
All: no cross-model alignment levels or causes.

record.verdict_notes: The relation is changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only'. Convergent Learning (an original source) appears only in the reference list, and Kornblith's CKA is used as a tool. All rows are within-model, figure-only, and carry no numeric values.

versions.untested_parts: Not tested: alignment between independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data as model size and capability increase.
Not tested: alignment of vision and language models on paired images and captions as both models improve.
Not tested: shared features or subspaces across independently initialized networks of the same architecture.
Not tested: mapping or stitching representations across models, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
Not tested: recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across different models.
Not tested: whether cross-model convergence changes with similarity metric, metric settings, or input distribution.
Not tested: whether cross-model alignment is incomplete or explained by shared training data or objectives.
